title: Simultaneous K-injective models and diagram descent for direct-image/open words
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. On small representatives of the small pro-etale sites of schemes in a common universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and $\mathcal M_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$. Use the module direct images $a_*$, inverse images $a^*$ and their specified adjunctions [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and the exact open extension by zero $j_!\dashv j^*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. Assume the canonical coefficient maps $\alpha_a:a^{-1}\Lambda_T\to\Lambda_S$ are isomorphisms for the morphisms under consideration; identify module inverse image with sheaf inverse image whose action is transported by $\alpha_a^{-1}$.
Write $Q_T:K(\mathcal M_T)\to D(\mathcal M_T)$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. A complex $I$ is K-injective when every map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null-homotopic [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Consider any finite collection of composable words $w=F_m\cdots F_1$ whose letters are module direct images $a_*$ or module restrictions $j^*$ along open immersions, including empty words. Let $w^{\mathrm d}$ replace $a_*$ by its total right derived functor and $j^*$ by its exact induced functor. Then:

(i) Every complex of $\mathcal M_T$ has a K-injective resolution; every letter and every word carries K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes. Under the section-ring equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], these are the same representatives and functors as for ordinary module sheaves.

(ii) For a K-injective resolution $a:N\to I$ there are canonical evaluation isomorphisms $e_{w,a}:w^{\mathrm d}(Q_SN)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_T(wI)$, formed from the derived units at each successive K-injective image. For $h:Q_SN\to Q_SN'$ and another resolution $b:N'\to J$, let $t:I\to J$ represent the unique homotopy class with $Q_St=(Q_Sb)h(Q_Sa)^{-1}$. Then
$$e_{w,b}\,w^{\mathrm d}(h)\,e_{w,a}^{-1}=Q_T(wt).$$
For a second resolution $a':N\to I'$, $e_{w,a'}e_{w,a}^{-1}=Q_T(wu)$, where $Q_Su=(Q_Sa')(Q_Sa)^{-1}$; these transitions satisfy the cocycle equation.

(iii) Any natural transformation $\theta:w\to v$ of underived words with the same endpoints induces a unique natural transformation $\theta^{\mathrm d}:w^{\mathrm d}\to v^{\mathrm d}$ satisfying
$$e_{v,a}\,\theta^{\mathrm d}_{Q_SN}\,e_{w,a}^{-1}=Q_T(\theta_I).$$
This formula is independent of the resolution and of homotopic representatives. If $\theta$ is an isomorphism, so is $\theta^{\mathrm d}$. It preserves identities, vertical composition and whiskering by any allowed word, using the canonical evaluation identifications. Consequently every finite equality of composites and whiskerings of underived transformations between these words gives the corresponding equality on the unbounded derived categories, with their canonical associators. No exactness of $a_*$ and no boundedness or constructibility of the complexes is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined. Agent formulation of simultaneous word evaluation and transformation-diagram descent, extracted from old steps 1, 2 and 5 of lem-sfb-derived-direct-image-open-coherence

proof.text: Use the additive exact section-ring equivalences $E_T$ and the comparisons for direct images, inverse images and open adjunctions of [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport]. On the stipulated small sites, [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] gives a K-injective resolution of every sectionwise module complex. Exactness of $E_T$ and its inverse identifies acyclic complexes. Additivity transports the equation $f=dh+hd$ degree by degree, and full faithfulness identifies the maps from each acyclic complex. Hence a complex is K-injective exactly when its image under $E_T$ is, and the resolutions transfer back. The same comparisons identify the specified operations on these representatives. This proves the existence and section-ring assertion of (i); here 'same' is through the canonical comparisons, not a literal equality of the two categories.

source.place: Section 07A5 (section-unbounded); Theorem 079P (injectives-theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck), applied through the section-ring equivalence

proof.text: For a scheme morphism $a$, the adjunction $a^*\dashv a_*$ is the specified one in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and its left adjoint is additive exact by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] to obtain preservation by $a_*$. For an open $j$, [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] gives the exact left adjoint $j_!$ of $j^*$; apply the same lemma to this adjunction to obtain preservation by $j^*$. No exactness of the right adjoint $a_*$ is used.

source.place: Tag 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives), once for each kind of letter

proof.text: Induct on word length: the empty word fixes $I$, and if $uI$ is K-injective then $F(uI)$ is K-injective by the letter result of step 2. This proves preservation for every word. All letters are additive. If $t-t'=dh+hd$, degreewise application of any letter gives $F(t)-F(t')=dF(h)+F(h)d$; iterating proves that every word acts on homotopy classes. In particular it sends a homotopy equivalence and its chosen inverse homotopies to a homotopy equivalence. These observations also apply to the empty word.

source.place: Tag 08BJ: iteration of the preservation assertion, and the defining homotopy equation

proof.text: For a letter $F=a_*$, [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] supplies the isomorphism $\epsilon_{F,L}:F^{\mathrm d}(QL)\to Q(FL)$ for K-injective $L$, namely the inverse derived unit using the identity resolution of $L$. It also supplies $\epsilon_{F,L'}F^{\mathrm d}(Qs)\epsilon_{F,L}^{-1}=Q(Fs)$ for a map $s:L\to L'$ between K-injectives. For $F=j^*$ the exact induced functor has $F^{\mathrm d}Q=QF$ with its canonical factorization identification, so the same equation follows by its defining action on maps, and $\epsilon_{F,L}$ is that identification. Thus both kinds of letter have the same evaluation rule.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), with arbitrary-resolution map formula; exact restrictions use their induced-functor definition

proof.text: Construct the evaluations by induction. For the empty word put $e_{1,a}=Qa$. If $w=Fu$, define $e_{Fu,a}=\epsilon_{F,uI}\circ F^{\mathrm d}(e_{u,a})$. Step 3 verifies that $uI$ is K-injective, so step 4 applies at every stage. Every factor is invertible. This definition is precisely iteration of the derived units, with the exact-induced identifications for restriction letters. It works simultaneously for all the specified words using the one initial resolution $a:N\to I$.

source.place: Tag 070Y: recursive use of the evaluation at a K-injective complex

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], the derived arrow $(Qb)h(Qa)^{-1}:QI\to QJ$ lifts to one and only one homotopy class $t:I\to J$. Prove the formula of (ii) by induction on $w$. For the empty word it is this defining equality. For $w=Fu$, substitute the formula for $u$ into the recursive evaluations: the conjugated map becomes $\epsilon_{F,uJ}F^{\mathrm d}(Q(ut))\epsilon_{F,uI}^{-1}$, which is $Q(Fut)$ by the one-letter computation of step 4. The latter is exactly the identity-resolution specialization of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] for a direct-image letter; for an exact restriction it is the defining map formula. This proves the assertion for arbitrary derived arrows, rather than just arrows of complexes.

Apply step 6 with $h=1_{QN}$ and $b=a'$ to obtain $e_{w,a'}e_{w,a}^{-1}=Q(wu)$. The reverse transition lifts the inverse derived arrow; [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] implies that both composites are identity homotopy classes. Thus $u$ is a homotopy equivalence, and step 3 shows that $wu$ is also one. For three resolutions the product of the two lifted transitions equals the third by that same bijectivity; applying $w$ and $Q$ gives the cocycle equation. This also shows explicitly why applying a possibly nonexact direct image to these transition maps is legitimate.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), bijectivity on maps into K-injectives

proof.text: For an underived natural transformation $\theta:w\to v$, its degreewise components on a complex form a chain map: $\theta_{I^{n+1}}w(d^n)=v(d^n)\theta_{I^n}$ is naturality for $d^n$. For a complex $N$ with resolution $a$, define $\theta^{\mathrm d}_{QN}=e_{v,a}^{-1}Q(\theta_I)e_{w,a}$. For a change of resolution represented by $u:I\to I'$, naturality gives $v(u)\theta_I=\theta_{I'}w(u)$. Substitute the transition formulas of step 7; the two choices of $a$ give the same component. This construction uses only a representative complex for each derived object, which exists by the localization definition. If a localization model uses isomorphic objects, transport the component along that isomorphism; the arbitrary-arrow naturality checked next makes this transport independent.

source.place: Tags 070I and 070Y: agent construction using the evaluation formulas and naturality of the given transformation

proof.text: For $h:QN\to QN'$ choose the homotopy class $t:I\to J$ of step 6. The desired naturality square, conjugated by its four evaluation isomorphisms, is $Q(vt)Q(\theta_I)=Q(\theta_J)Q(wt)$, which follows from naturality of $\theta$ on the chain map $t$. Changing $t$ by a homotopy changes neither side by step 3. This proves naturality for every derived arrow and independence of all homotopic choices. The evaluation formula determines every component on every object, so it determines a unique natural transformation. If $\theta$ is invertible, applying the construction to $\theta^{-1}$ gives its inverse by cancellation of the evaluations.

source.place: Tags 070I and 070Y: conjugation of naturality by the established arbitrary-arrow formula

proof.text: For identities and vertical composites, conjugation cancels the middle evaluation, giving respectively $Q(1_{wI})$ and $Q(\psi_I\theta_I)$. To check whiskering, first note the concatenation formula $e_{ux,a}=e_{u,1_{xI}}\circ u^{\mathrm d}(e_{x,a})$, where $xI$ is K-injective. Induction on the length of $u$ proves it directly from step 5: for $u=1$ it is $e_{x,a}$, and adding $F$ inserts $\epsilon_{F,uxI}$ on both sides. Right whiskering $\theta x$ therefore evaluates to $Q(\theta_{xI})$, since $xI$ may use its identity resolution. Left whiskering $y\theta$ evaluates to $Q(y\theta_I)$ by step 6 applied to the map $\theta_I:wI\to vI$ between the K-injective word images. These are exactly the underived whiskerings evaluated on $I$. Thus both whiskerings and vertical composition are preserved with the canonical evaluation identifications.

source.place: Tag 070Y: finite induction on evaluation for concatenated words and conjugation of transformations

proof.text: Evaluate a finite composite-and-whiskering expression on a common $I$. Step 10 identifies its value with $Q$ of the corresponding underived expression at $I$. Equal underived expressions therefore have equal evaluated values. Cancel the source and target evaluation isomorphisms to obtain equality on each derived object, hence equality of natural transformations. Reparenthesizing inserts only the canonical functor associators: their components identify $(Fu)I$ with $F(uI)$, and the concatenation calculation of step 10 gives the same evaluation on either side. This proves the final diagram assertion, including identity letters, empty words and all canonical associators. All resolutions and map computations above are unbounded, and no support or constructibility condition has entered.

source.place: Tag 070Y: conclusion of the finite word evaluation argument

proof_origin.place: Tags 08BJ, 070I and 070Y; explicit finite-word induction and natural-transformation descent from these results, with existence from sites-cohomology Section 07A5 and injectives Theorem 079P.

lean.statement: theorem word_diagram_descent : (∀ {S T : Scheme.{u}} {w v : Word S T} (e : Expression Λ w v), e.derived Λ = Word.cell Λ (e.ordinary Λ)) ∧ (∀ {S T : Scheme.{u}} {w v : Word S T} (e f : Expression Λ w v), e.ordinary Λ = f.ordinary Λ → e.derived Λ = f.derived Λ) ∧ (∀ {S T : Scheme.{u}} {w v : Word S T} (θ : w.ordinary Λ ⟶ v.ordinary Λ), IsIso θ → IsIso (Word.cell Λ θ))
lean.note: The declarations together render all three clauses.
